subject: grad
title: GRAD.------DOC.
description: Diagram in WI-11, the section where Braxton introduces the *gradualism* concept by way of the talk-show anecdote about a white jazz musician who named Tony Bennett the best jazz singer in history, Woody Herman's the best big band, etc. — illustrating how 'the perpetuation of a given viewpoint, in a given time parameter, can be solidified as true, if not successfully challenged.' (C)GRAD (gradualism) is crossed with DOC (documentation): the diagram poses what gradualism actually does to documentation. DOC → GRAD (the crossing), and DOC → DEF (definition). DEF → INFO-INTR (information interpretation), which fans to POL-SIGN (political significance) and INT (intention). CULT-INFO-F (culture information focus) also feeds INT — meaning intention is over-determined by both information-interpretation and culture-information-focus. GRAD outputs to TRS (transition) → PART (participation) and to PHY-U-P (physical universe particular) → RT-DY (reality dynamics). Structural argument: gradualism is downstream of documentation, but its productive outputs are transition into participation and physical-universe → reality-dynamics — i.e., gradualism actually *changes* what counts as participatory and as real. Definition's chain through information-interpretation produces both political significance and intention (intention being the convergence with culture-information-focus). The diagram thus diagrams the structure Braxton identifies: 'Paul Whiteman, King of Jazz' is not a slip — it's documentation feeding definition feeding information-interpretation, with political-significance as one terminal and intention as another. Once intention is captured by culture-information-focus, gradualism's transition→participation and physical-universe→reality-dynamics outputs operate to *materialize* the captured definition.
